title: OpsPlaybook scheduler and idempotent Admin SDK adapter
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Summary: Build an OpsPlaybook scheduler and an adapter layer for the Admin SDK so runbooks can be executed as idempotent, auditable tasks. This ticket combines three related pieces: (1) a lightweight scheduler to run periodic/cron runbook tasks, (2) an Admin SDK adapter that exposes safe, permission-checked operations as idempotent actions callable from the scheduler and support tooling, and (3) a migration plan to convert high-value runbooks into task objects with observability and retry semantics.

Goals: 1) Allow runbooks to be treated as first-class tasks (traceable, retryable, rate-limited). 2) Provide an adapter in the Admin SDK that enforces RBAC and produces structured audit events for every admin action. 3) Implement a scheduler service that supports locked execution, backoff/retry, and dry-run mode for validation. 4) Provide developer CLI commands to convert existing runbooks into tasks and to run them interactively.

Non-goals: This ticket will not implement a full UI for scheduling or tenancy separation (those are follow-ups). We will not modify on-call routing; only provide hooks for webhooks to notify paging systems.

Design notes and trade-offs: - Scheduler: lean, single-replica coordinator with leader election (uses existing k8s leader lease) to avoid creating another HA system. Chosen because ops runbooks are low-frequency and leader election reduces operational burden. - Idempotency: each adapter action accepts an explicit idempotency key; for legacy runbook steps where the action cannot be made strictly idempotent, the adapter will emulate idempotency using a pre/post-check pattern and a reversible marker in audit events. This increases complexity but is necessary to guarantee safe reruns. - Observability: every task emits structured events to the existing ops-events Kafka topic and a summarized trace in Console under "Ops Tasks" for per-route latency/cost. We considered writing directly to the Console DB but opted for events->ingest path to reuse existing pipelines.

Migration plan: - Phase 1 (this ticket): implement adapter + scheduler + CLI converter + update 3 high-priority runbooks (db-maintenance, certificate-rotation, cache-eviction) as proof-of-concept. - Phase 2: bulk convert remaining curated runbooks, add UI controls and tenant scoping. - Phase 3: add canary/AB scheduling and integration with Dedicated autoscaler policies.

APIs and artifacts: - Admin SDK adapter RFC: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/OPSPlaybook+Adapter+RFC
- Prototype CLI: github.com/redwood-inference/admin-cli/tree/opsplaybook-scheduler (PR #8421)
- POC scheduler helm chart: github.com/redwood-inference/charts/tree/opsplaybook-scheduler
- Runbook examples to convert: drive.redwood.com/ops/runbooks/maintenance-catalog

Operational concerns: - Audit log retention & KMS: ensure audit payloads are encrypted through KMS path. - RBAC: adapter must verify caller scopes using SSO tokens and fallback service account mapping for scheduled tasks. - Rate limiting: long-running tasks should be rate-limited per-tenant to avoid saturation.

Next steps: complete adapter unit tests, land PR for scheduler core, run POC conversion of db-maintenance runbook, and schedule internal dry-run for safety checks.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler binary deploys with leader election and exposes /healthz and /metrics
Admin SDK exposes adapter methods with RBAC checks and logs structured audit events to ops-events topic
Converted runbooks (db-maintenance, certificate-rotation, cache-eviction) execute via scheduler in dry-run and real-run modes with idempotency verified
CLI provides convert/run commands and generates a task manifest saved to repo for review
Automated tests for adapter idempotency and scheduler backoff coverage included in CI
Documentation and runbook migration guide published in Confluence
